stories.title: Thousands await aid after deadly Indonesian earthquake
stories.summary: Thousands of evacuees waited for help on Indonesia's island of Flores after a powerful earthquake killed 51 people, injured dozens and damaged hundreds of houses and buildings. Thirty-six people were seriously injured in the quake in East Nusa Tenggara province, while 77 had minor injuries, Deputy Health Minister Benjamin Paulus Octavianus told a televised meeting. Some 5,000 people fled their homes as the 7.7-magnitude quake hit the island early yesterday, followed by 341 aftershocks in the hours that followed, a spokesman for the BNPB national disaster agency, Berton Suar Pelita Panjaitan, said. People in some areas were left without electricity and telecommunications and at least one emergency access road remained inaccessible.

stories.title: I-RES sees slight revenue increase, profits jump
stories.summary: Ireland's largest private landlord, Irish Residential Properties REIT (I-RES) has posted its interim results for the first half of the year, saying strong operational and strategic delivery drove earning growth and shareholder returns. The company saw a slight increase in its revenues year on year - it booked €43.1m euro in the six month period, up 1.1 percent on the same period of last year. The group posted a profit before tax of €48 million versus €16.3 million in the prior period. It said this was driven by the non-cash fair value movement of its assets which was underpinned by performance of the portfolio and stable yields.

stories.title: 111 people detained after fresh Ceuta crossing attempt
stories.summary: Moroccan authorities have detained 111 people in and around the northern city of Fnideq after they attempted a mass crossing into Spain's city of Ceuta. A Fnideq provincial official said 109 of those detained today were from African countries and two were Moroccan nationals. A heavy security presence prevented any mass crossing near Ceuta and Melilla, with the security situation remaining "normal and under control," the official said. Authorities will continue monitoring online activity to identify people involved in encouraging mass migration attempts, while field operations will continue to prevent irregular crossings and detain those organising them, the official said.

stories.title: Sligo Rovers see off fearless Kerry FC to progress
stories.summary: There was to be no repeat of last year's heroics as a fearless Kerry were knocked out of the Club Orange Men's FAI Cup by a Sligo Rovers side who reached the last eight for the second year running. Cian Kavanagh hit the opener at the Showgrounds, while Alex Nolan converted a penalty before the break. The scoreline was harsh on Kerry, who were well on top for the majority of the second period and will wonder how they didn't score at least, as a reel of superb Sam Sargeant stops kept the visitors scoreless before Carl McHugh and debutant Kaiyne Woolery settled the tie with late goals. The Showgrounds has been a venue of much change in recent weeks, with Darren Purse and Warren Feeney taking charge of the first team following the departure of former manager John Russell and his assistant Ryan Casey to Shelbourne. Club captain Will Fitzgerald was bought by Shamrock Rovers, while Purse has brought in four new players to help Rovers pull off a great escape from relegation.

stories.title: Croke Park keen to host annual Premier League friendlies
stories.summary: Croke Park chiefs are keen to make Premier League pre-season friendlies like Wednesday night's clash between Manchester United and Leeds regular events. The match between the long-standing rivals was the first game of soccer to be played at the home of the GAA since 2009, but was seen as a huge success as a sell-out crowd of 75,000 watched Manchester United beat their old rivals on penalties. The only previous times soccer had been played at the venue were between 2007 and 2009 when it served as the temporary home of the Republic of Ireland during the redevelopment of Lansdowne Road. But Peter McKenna, Croke Park’s stadium and commercial director, is keen to change that to find new revenue streams to put into the GAA.

stories.summary: Robbie Williams has opened up about overcoming a "huge amount of imposter syndrome", saying he has reached a point in his life where he feels incredibly "lucky" and "grateful" to be doing what he does. The former Take That star, who is set to play two gigs at Limerick's Thomond Park next summer, reflected on how his attitude towards his career and success has changed as he has got older. "There was a huge amount of imposter syndrome, a huge amount of 'I was in a boyband and I’m lucky to be and how dare I, and who do I think I am thinking that I am someone I can’t be etc.’" Williams said that, with age, he has learned to let go of those feelings and appreciate the position he finds himself in.

Mr Farage won with 22,239 votes, with Count Binface in second place on 9,455 votes. Mr Farage secured a 12,784 majority, 62.82% of the vote. This is up from his 8,405 vote majority, 46.2%, when he won at the 2024 general election. The result was declared shortly after 6am. A total of 32 of the record-34 candidates lost their deposit.

stories.title: KPMG Australia faces more whistleblower misconduct claims
stories.summary: "Many, many more" whistleblowers have come forward with reports of misconduct at KPMG Australia, a parliamentary committee probing alleged client data leaks at the firm heard on ‌Friday, raising concerns about a broader pattern of wrongdoing. The scandal erupted in March following allegations made by an anonymous whistleblower that KPMG misused confidential client information to bid for audit contracts. KPMG initially said the claims were unsubstantiated. But the firm's CEO, audit boss and chairman have all since resigned, and it has confirmed the misuse of internal documents by staff. At a parliamentary hearing in Canberra, Deborah O'Neill, a Labor party senator who chairs the committee, said more people were now reporting similar conduct.

stories.title: Hopes fade for survivors following Colombia earthquake
stories.summary: Hopes of finding survivors of the earthquake ⁠that struck western Colombia five days ago are dwindling, as more bodies were pulled from buildings that collapsed due to the 7.4-magnitude quake that left hundreds dead or missing. The earthquake struck in San Jose del Palmar, toppling apartment buildings and damaging schools, churches, hospitals and homes from the Pacific port Buenaventurato in Colombia's coffee-growing region and major western cities. Colombia's disaster management unit has estimated that at least 294 people have died with 320 more missing and nearly 4,000 more injured. Over two-thirds of the deaths were concentrated in the cities of Cali and Pereira.

stories.title: Scheffler in control as Irish duo struggle in Memphis
stories.summary: Scottie Scheffler closed in on just his second win of the season at the FedEx St. Jude Championship, as Shane Lowry and Rory McIlroy suffered another stagnant afternoon. The world number one carded a third round of two-under-par 68 to take a two shot head into the final day's play, sitting on 13-under. The FedEx Cup leader failed to find the same momentum as his Friday 61, mixing four birdies with two bogeys. He will go off in the final group on Sunday alongside Ryder Cup teammate Sam Burns who fired his own low round of the week, an eight-under-par 62, with Sungjae Im also in a tie for second place on 11-under. It would prove to be a costly and frustrating day for both Shane Lowry and Rory McIlroy however, who both carded two-over-par rounds to slip further back.

stories.title: Offaly's All-Ireland winning captain Pádraig Horan dies
stories.summary: Pádraig Horan, who captained Offaly to their first All-Ireland hurling success in 1981, has died at the age of 76 after a long battle with illness. In a lengthy inter-county career which began at the end of the 1960s, Horan was to the fore as the Faithful famously shocked Kilkenny to win a maiden Leinster title in 1980s. Offaly had arrived, with the St Ryangh's clubman adding three more provincial crowns and another Liam MacCarthy success, in 1985, to his collection. His exploits on the field, first as a defender before moving to the full-forward berth, were also recognised when he was named on the All-Star team for '85. As a coach, he managed Offaly to win a National League title in 1991, while four years later he was at the helm when Birr landed All-Ireland senior club honours.

stories.title: Arteta: Nothing to worry about with contract extension
stories.summary: Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta has promised fans they have nothing to worry about regarding his contract situation and insisted everyone at the club is "comfortable" about extending his deal soon. After Arteta ended the Gunners' 22-year wait for Premier League title success in May, new terms were expected to be finalised between the Spaniard and the club quickly after the conclusion of last season. However, with Arsenal set to begin their 2026-27 campaign with the Community Shield against Manchester City in Cardiff on Sunday, there have been minimal updates on the long-term future of Arteta, who has entered the final 12 months of his contract. Yet, Arteta said: "They (Arsenal fans) don’t have to worry about any of that, because I want to be here.

stories.title: Leinster and Connacht ring the changes
stories.summary: Leinster head coach Sana Govender hands four players their provincial debut for Saturday's Vodafone Interprovincial Championship clash with Connacht at Energia Park. In total there are six changes from last week's defeat to Munster. To ease him through his final days, Dr. Josef Alois calls for someone from his past. Enter Catherine Carolan, now an Oxford professor. A novel in two strands, A Thought without Collision is a meditation on how we construct our relationship to the world around us.

stories.summary: From the mouth-watering Big Grill Festival in Herbert Park to the street culture RePlay Festival in Tallaght, there is plenty happening in Dublin this weekend. Taking place on Saturday, 15 August, at Parthalán Place, the festival will bring together skaters, DJs, dancers, graffiti artists and performers from across Ireland for a full-day takeover. Running from 10am - 6pm, you can expect skate and BMX showcases, roller skating displays, live DJs, rap cyphers, spoken word, street dance, outdoor games and workshops where everyone can try out street sports and creative activities alongside professionals. Celebrate 10 years of laughs with a mighty night of comedy at the Pearse Centre. For their 10-year anniversary, Auto-Correbt is going to perform everything they've ever done (as best as they can remember it). This is an improvised comedy show, which means that everything is made up on the spot and no one knows what's going to happen next. Tickets from €9.01. Running from Wednesday, 12 August - Thursday, 20 August, Dublin music venue and bar Whelan's will hot the 2026 Trad & Folk Festival. stories.title: €23m spent on Assessment of Need challenges since 2021
stories.summary: The State has spent over €23 million in legal costs arising from Assessments of Need (AON) challenges since 2021, new figures have revealed. Under the Disability Act 2005, parents can take a case against the HSE if they do not receive an assessment report for their child with special needs within a six-month timeframe, if they are unhappy with the outcome of the assessment or if they feel the service was below par. An AON is a formal legal process carried out by the HSE to identify a child's health and educational needs stemming from a disability, and to determine the appropriate public services required to meet those needs. However, there are too few specialists in the system and lengthy waiting lists have become the norm.

stories.title: Questions over finances remain as Farage wins by-election
stories.summary: Local MP Nigel Farage was widely predicted to win the by-election he caused when he gave up his seat amid mounting questions over donations and gifts he received worth millions of pounds. Mr Farage says he did nothing wrong, that a £5 million donation from Thailand-based cryptocurrency billionaire Christopher Harborne was for his personal security. But under a code of conduct governing donations to Members of the British Parliament, any gifts given to newly elected MPs in the year before they are elected must be declared. So, an investigation was opened by the Parliamentary Standards Commissioner into the matter.

stories.title: Oil set for weekly gains
stories.summary: Oil prices were mixed today but set for weekly gains after the US threatened an indefinite naval blockade of Iran, raising concerns about disruptions to crude supplies from the Middle East. Brent futures were down 12 cents, or 0.1%, to $86.95 a barrel this afternoon, while US West Texas Intermediate crude futures were up 13 cents, or 0.2%, to $81.38 a barrel. Brent and WTI were on track for weekly gains of about 3.4% and 4%, respectively. Higher oil prices are a natural result of the latest approach by the US, which implies little hope of a near-term resolution in the Middle East, said Bjarne Schieldrop, chief analyst for commodities at SEB Research.

stories.title: Athlone remain top despite impressive Sligo performance
stories.summary: Athlone Town remain the pace setters at the top having been pushed all the way by an impressive Sligo Rovers in a game full of excitement. First-half goals from player-of-the-match Izzy Ryan and Alexis Strckland had the league leaders in the driving seat but they were made to pay for some slack finishing as Sligo Rovers stunned the title favourites. The visitors drew level through a Hannah Waesch own goal and a Cara Jordan stunner - only for Strickland to grab a dramatic 90th minute winner. Looking for what would have been their first ever win over last season's double winners, Gavin Hughes' well coached side proved why they are one of the in-form teams in the country but ultimately saw their nine-game unbeaten run come to an end. Despite the home side missing star winger Madie Gibson, and much like they did last week at Wexford, they proved their strength and depth again bringing in the lightning quick Ryan on the left who was a constant threat from the first whistle to last.

stories.title: Donegal All-Ireland winner McHugh, wife killed in crash
stories.summary: Former Donegal 1992 All-Ireland winning football star James McHugh and his wife Noreen have died following a road traffic collision which happened in Co Cavan yesterday afternoon. The Cill Chartha native, who was in his early 60s, was fatally injured in the crash which involved a car and a van on the N3 at Drummallaght, between Virginia and Cavan town. Noreen McHugh, who was a passenger in the car, was seriously injured and airlifted to Beaumont Hospital for treatment. She died in hospital this evening. The driver of the van, a man in his 50s, was taken to hospital to be treated for minor injuries.
